VKF 0.1.8 — Compact Indexing And Pipe Assignment

VKF 0.1.8 makes the compact source style part of the verified compiler surface.

Language And Compiler

  • values.index selects a vector position when index is a bound int or num.
  • values.(expression) remains the form for computed indices, multiple indices, and special values such as $.
  • A range pipe may contain indexed assignment directly:
  ..n - 1 >> working.($): permutation.($)
  • The assignment runs once per range element. If another >> follows, it receives the value that was stored by the preceding assignment.
  • Record fields remain ordinary named fields. Compact dynamic indexing is only selected when the left value is a vector and the right name is a bound numeric index.

Canonical Examples And Documentation

  • The Fannkuch copy and shift loops now use range pipes instead of manually declared and incremented loop indices.
  • Discarded finite range pipes lower to counted machine loops without allocating or concatenating a result vector.
  • Public benchmark, guide, architecture, and example sources use .index for simple bound indices and retain parentheses only for computed indices.
  • The landing README now includes a basic syntax reference and a complete while-loop plus repeated-match example with exact output.

Native Optimization

  • Numeric functions whose only errors terminate the function can retain hot scalar locals in registers; catchable errors and owned values keep the conservative stack-backed path.
  • Floating locals used as indexed-address operands are excluded from the register cache, preventing stale stack indices under tuner-selected policies.
  • Call-free SysV x64 numeric functions cache hot values in XMM8 through XMM15; XMM0 through XMM7 remain reserved for expression and scratch lowering.

Verification

  • The native VKF suite includes regressions for range-pipe indexed assignment, compact named indexing, and assignment values piped onward.
  • The Windows x64 native suite reports 323 passed, 0 failed.
  • Every documented program is compiled from 10 fresh paths and executed in 10 fresh operating-system processes on Windows x64, Linux x64, and macOS ARM64.
  • Every round must return the same exit code and byte-identical stdout and stderr. This release does not use per-example timing as a quality claim.
  • The controlled Linux x64 comparison uses the 0.1.8 compiler, 50 warmups, and 1,000 measured raw samples per language and kernel. Every VKF/C, VKF/Rust, and VKF/Zig ratio is below 2× across spectral norm, Fannkuch, and N-body.
  • Full samples, hashes, toolchains, and machine conditions are stored in linux-x64-018-controlled-1000.json.

VKF remains an unsupported experimental preview. physics, ui, and symbolic are still excluded from the native release.
